findings.title: Preserve the complete original generated-grid algorithm
findings.mechanism: Host generation stops after initial point sampling and retains sea sentinel-5000. Original terrsel.c then processes coastal intersections and replaces remaining-5000 with sea_height-1=-2. The new SEA test asserts the intermediate-5000 value rather than original final behavior. Independently read original generated files contain zero-5000posts and257456/394360posts at-2. The existing sweep test also still expects fast_available0 after its map now gains a generated grid, so it will fail on the new behavior.
findings.bounded_correction: Port the full original coast/postprocessing/read order into the host, including required host-owned coastal input services, without delegating the calculation to the DLL. Preserve original byte oracles and correct the sea/fast_available assertions. Then compare full generated data and original fast hashes on both controlled missing-file variants; do not declare the gap closed from a flat-land test.

findings.title: Reject an answer variant that does not match its terrain operation
findings.mechanism: terrain_callback derives TerrainQuery from source.op but matches TerrainAnswer independently. A safe Rust provider can answer Map or Fast to a POINT request; otherwise-zero point fields reach C, whose finite/type checks accept elevation0/normal0/type0/nil-hint. This fabricates a successful physical reply instead of refusing. Lua normally constructs the correct variant, so this is the public Rust/generic-host/native bridge seam, not an observed Lua native failure.
findings.bounded_correction: Validate the (request op,answer variant) pair before writing reply_out. Refuse every mismatched pair with a clear requested-operation marker, preserving valid variants. Test the actual callback/serialization path and prove no reply application on rejection.

findings.title: Select the same actual boot season in the reference host
findings.mechanism: All32new script registrations omit winter, and install_provider maps omission tofalse before native boot. Native set_current_game_session calls notify_session_parameters, which reads map_info and sets the season before the loader chooses default-W.sec when both winter files exist. Valid winter maps can therefore use winter DLL sector data and summer host point geometry silently; sector-count equality does not distinguish those maps.
findings.bounded_correction: Select/transport the actual original boot season at the correct point, or explicitly refuse an unsupported mismatch. Preserve winter-pair fallback semantics and distinguish season-dependent cache keys. Exercise distinct summer/winter file fixtures; no winter native coverage is claimed from the supplied summer controls.

findings.title: Keep semantic record validity independent of optional opaque cache state
findings.mechanism: face_stored becomes true only if the point answer carries a nonempty hint. A valid generic no-hint surface answer never makes has_face true despite populating elevation/normal/type. Both fixed-wing death/contact paths consequently treat populated data as invalid and issue extra queries each call; sampling/order depends on exposing a cache token rather than physical facts.
findings.bounded_correction: Represent semantic stored-surface/record validity separately from optional cache hints, preserving original reference stale/no-face behavior with explicit by-value metadata if needed. A valid generic no-hint reply must establish usable data without a fake EECH hint. Cover actual client validity/predicate behavior and clear/refill cases.

findings.title: Qualify retained hashes and solver-symbol checks precisely
findings.mechanism: The comment says point hashes remain comparable, but fold_answer includes fast_hit in word6 and the new client always reportsFALSE. Primed hashes can therefore change solely from the lost internal diagnostic even when physical tuples match. Separately README requires system_point_data absence although the new client legitimately defines a shared value cache under that name.
findings.bounded_correction: Distinguish physical tuple/sample comparison from diagnostic-containing primed/run hashes; preserve originals and classify deltas explicitly. Do not require optional host diagnostics or legacy solver echoes. Check object ownership and absence of original numerical triangle/scratch-reference code rather than banning the valid client shared-cache name.

ownership_and_memory_assessment.dispatch: EECH_CAMPAIGN_HOST_TERRAIN excludes the old terrelev numerical body and the legacy terrsel fast lookup; mb_hostterrain implements public point/fast/record operations solely through the required callback. No hidden DLL point/fast solver fallback was found. Legacy code text remains for the original game, not the active headless numerical dispatch.
ownership_and_memory_assessment.values: Terrain requests/replies and opaque bounded hint strings cross by value. Legacy record pointers are replaced by private C values; raw address/entity heap ID/seed/layout does not cross the public Lua boundary.32reference scripts explicitly register terrain; no automatic module-global default provider is used.
ownership_and_memory_assessment.generation_lock: Terrain::from_bytes now holds the same all-map C_SOLVER lock across open/generation. The new generation calls its C point body directly inside that interval, so the earlier global-static race is not reintroduced. Generated allocation is owned/freed by the C map; grid byte buffers remain alive as needed. No additional pointer-lifetime or allocation-bounds defect was established in this pass.
ownership_and_memory_assessment.retention: BOOTED.swap at the start prevents a second safe Rust boot from replacing the first provider. The owned TLS closure retains its Lua function; terrain_callback ignores transient with_host.user, so the retained C user address is not dereferenced by this Rust callback. try_borrow_mut and catch_unwind refuse reentrant borrowing/panics before C asks debug_fatal; fatal jumping occurs after the Rust callback returns. Provider retention includes failed native boot until thread/process end under the documented once-per-process model; it is not entry-scoped cleanup. This is an intentional resource-lifetime limit, not proof of post-failure recovery or a discovered UAF.
ownership_and_memory_assessment.abi: New request/reply and host callback field order match between C and repr(C) Rust by inspection. Actual32-bit size/alignment/all-inner-offset assertions were not supplied/executed for this new DTO set. Require relevant target ABI checks before final acceptance. No new representation mismatch was identified by source inspection.
ownership_and_memory_assessment.float_rng: Lua bridge validates fields before formatting/parsing and uses nearest_f32 for the callback rounding environment; fields/hints are copied without solver sanitation. New subnormal/negative-zero tests are source assertions, not an executed FE_TOWARDZERO native proof. No new campaign RNG draw/reordering was identified in the client. Original numeric generation is incomplete as findingGRID_POSTPROCESSING states.

remaining_D3_coupling: Native terrain/sector loader, type/cover/sector facts and trees remain G2/G3 data; core ground-impact geometry and contour/2D fast-grid generation remain compiled/active dependencies. Native sector-count matching is a declared transitional map constraint, not EECH-free DCS integration.
Active object/tree collision, device/sub-object viewpoints, target points/bounds, environmental/weather and host-time services remain finiteD3 work. They are not deferred toD5.
Shared value cache system_point_data is legitimate bookkeeping; it is not evidence that old numerical solving remains.
